content:
morgan: Heads-up — Grafana alert firing for hosted-eus1 GPU pool. Large p95 spikes across multiple routes; heatmap shows a 'striped' saturation pattern (tiling) across racks :eyes:

morgan: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/POOL/hosted-eus1-heatmap?orgId=1

dan: I'm on it. Are we seeing KV cache missstorms or just admission backpressure?

morgan: Initial look: KV cache miss rate up ~3x, admission queue length climbing, but CPU on proxies looks normal. The tiling isn't uniform — every other rack at ~95% utilization, neighbors at ~40%.

priya: That sounds like slot fragmentation + uneven refill. Could be recent image churn or node tagging drift. Any recent node churn events in eus1?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New image rollout "inference-runtime:v2024.11.2" started 2024-05-01T06:42Z targeting eus1 pool (batch 2/4).

dan: Ah — rollout batch 2/4. Possible rolling restart induced cold caches. Alex, can routing spillover be triggered intentionally to smooth this?

alex: We have spillover rules but they prefer capacity-aware routing; it won't trigger until headroom < 10% global. Right now some racks are starved while others are fine — routing sees enough free overall so it keeps sending to preferred racks.

morgan: TL;DR: per-rack imbalance + cold KV cache causing per-rack throttles and localized admission spikes. p95 shows sawtooth as requests bounce between hot and cold racks.

dan: Quick mitigation: pause the rollout for remaining batches, scale up ephemeral prewarm of image on underutilized racks, and temporarily lower route affinity for the crowded racks so spillover triggers earlier. I'll make the pause call.

priya: +1 on prewarm. I'll open a prewarm job to pull image and warm KV cache on the low-util nodes (small replica set). Command: ```kubectl -n hosted-eus1 apply -f prewarm-job.yaml```

alex: Also proposing to temporarily lower the routing affinity factor: set routing.affinity.window=30s -> 10s for eus1. That will make routing more responsive to short-term headroom shifts. We should revert after stabilization.

morgan: Can someone run a quick query for per-rack kv_cache_hit_ratio and admission_queue_len?

priya: Running: ```curl -s 'http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_hit_ratio%7Bregion%3D"eus1"%7D' | jq .data.result```

priya: Result (summary): racks a,c,e ~0.28 hit, racks b,d,f ~0.78 hit. Admission queues: a,c,e avg len 25, b,d,f avg len 6.

dan: That's pretty clear. Low-hit racks match high queue lengths. Prewarm + pause rollout now. I'm filing the pause and scaling ops.

ops-shift: Logged incident note: INC-2024-452. Added runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/tiling-saturation.md :thumbsup:

morgan: After prewarm kicks in we should see hit ratio converge and admission reduce. If not, escalate to cross-region spillover (route to usw2) and enable temporary rate-limiter increase on priority customers only.

alex: I'll change affinity and add a 1-hour scheduled rollback. Pushing change now: ```sh
curl -X POST https://routing-api.internal/config -d '{"region":"eus1","routing.affinity.window":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
```

infra-bot: ops: prewarm-job hosted-eus1 created by priya at 2024-05-01T06:58Z

priya: Prewarm logs showing successful image pull on racks a,c,e — KV caches warming. Hit ratios slowly trending up.

morgan: Nice. Keep monitoring for 15m. If p95 stays > 2s after 15m, we escalate to cross-region spillover.

dan: Pause confirmed for remaining rollout batches. Notifying release team.

ops-shift: Monitoring note added. Will update thread in 10 minutes. :clock10:

morgan: Thanks team. Good catch — tiling pattern might be our new hot failure mode after faster rollouts. Let's add a postmortem checklist item to validate per-rack cache warm before continuing future rollouts.

alex: Agreed. I'll file a short RFC for rollout prewarm policy and automatic affinity adjustments.

priya: Update: 12 minutes in — per-rack hit ratios: a,c,e -> 0.62, b,d,f -> 0.76. Admission queues dropping: a,c,e -> 8. p95 trending down to 1.1s.

morgan: Stabilizing. Marking as trending-resolved. Will leave the affinity tweak live for 1hr then rollback. Great run. :raised_hands:
